segments.spokenText: Part 3. Reviewing an interview project. You now have one minute to read questions 21 to 30.

Come in, Amira and Ben. I've read your proposal about independent shopkeepers. You've found an interesting question about how businesses adapt when a street changes, but I think we need to look closely at recruitment.
segments.sourceText: Come in, Amira and Ben. I’ve read your proposal about independent shopkeepers. You’ve found an interesting question about how businesses adapt when a street changes, but I think we need to look closely at recruitment.

segments.spokenText: We've made a list from the traders' association website. It seemed better than walking along the street and approaching whoever wasn't busy.
segments.sourceText: We’ve made a list from the traders' association website. It seemed better than walking along the street and approaching whoever wasn’t busy.

segments.spokenText: It's organised, certainly. But remember that the association includes only members. Shops that closed recently won't appear, and new businesses may not have joined. If you use it alone, you'll hear from a particular surviving group.
segments.sourceText: It’s organised, certainly. But remember that the association includes only members. Shops that closed recently won’t appear, and new businesses may not have joined. If you use it alone, you’ll hear from a particular surviving group.

segments.spokenText: We could add names from older street directories and contact the former owners where details are public. We can't guarantee they'll agree, but at least the recruitment frame wouldn't automatically exclude them.
segments.sourceText: We could add names from older street directories and contact the former owners where details are public. We can’t guarantee they’ll agree, but at least the recruitment frame wouldn’t automatically exclude them.

segments.spokenText: Should we ask the association chair to conduct the introductions? People know her, so perhaps they'd speak more freely.
segments.sourceText: Should we ask the association chair to conduct the introductions? People know her, so perhaps they’d speak more freely.

segments.spokenText: She can circulate an invitation. I wouldn't have her sitting in the interviews. A trader might hesitate to criticise a scheme the association supported. Make clear that the project isn't a performance review and that individual statements won't be sent to her.
segments.sourceText: She can circulate an invitation. I wouldn’t have her sitting in the interviews. A trader might hesitate to criticise a scheme the association supported. Make clear that the project isn’t a performance review and that individual statements won’t be sent to her.

segments.spokenText: Our draft starts with, 'How has the new pedestrian area improved your business?' I can see now that assumes an improvement.
segments.sourceText: Our draft starts with, 'How has the new pedestrian area improved your business?' I can see now that assumes an improvement.

segments.spokenText: We should ask what changed, if anything, and then invite positive and negative examples. Otherwise we'd be providing the conclusion in the question.
segments.sourceText: We should ask what changed, if anything, and then invite positive and negative examples. Otherwise we’d be providing the conclusion in the question.

segments.spokenText: Good. You'll also need to distinguish memory from records. Someone may recall fewer customers during construction, but sales figures could follow a different pattern. Ask whether records are available without making their participation depend on handing over private accounts.
segments.sourceText: Good. You’ll also need to distinguish memory from records. Someone may recall fewer customers during construction, but sales figures could follow a different pattern. Ask whether records are available without making their participation depend on handing over private accounts.

segments.spokenText: We planned an audio recording rather than trying to write everything while they speak. We'd ask permission first and offer a note-only interview if they prefer.
segments.sourceText: We planned an audio recording rather than trying to write everything while they speak. We’d ask permission first and offer a note-only interview if they prefer.

segments.spokenText: That's sensible. Explain where the file will be kept and when it will be deleted. Permission to talk to you is not permission to put a voice recording on a public website.
segments.sourceText: That’s sensible. Explain where the file will be kept and when it will be deleted. Permission to talk to you is not permission to put a voice recording on a public website.

segments.spokenText: Now look at questions 26 to 30.
We made a checklist of remaining tasks. For the recruitment invitation, we need approval from you before sending it. We've drafted it but haven't contacted anyone yet.
segments.sourceText: We made a checklist of remaining tasks. For the recruitment invitation, we need approval from you before sending it. We’ve drafted it but haven’t contacted anyone yet.

segments.spokenText: Send it after this meeting. The interview schedule is different: its wording needs a trial. Ask somebody outside the final sample to respond, so you can see whether the order makes sense and how long it takes.
segments.sourceText: Send it after this meeting. The interview schedule is different: its wording needs a trial. Ask somebody outside the final sample to respond, so you can see whether the order makes sense and how long it takes.

segments.spokenText: The street map is finished. We've marked present businesses and former addresses from the directories, and checked that none of the symbols hides the street names.
segments.sourceText: The street map is finished. We’ve marked present businesses and former addresses from the directories, and checked that none of the symbols hides the street names.

segments.spokenText: Fine, treat that as completed for now. Don't spend another day improving its colours at the expense of preparation.
segments.sourceText: Fine, treat that as completed for now. Don’t spend another day improving its colours at the expense of preparation.

segments.spokenText: We also had a question asking each trader for their exact annual income. It doesn't answer our revised question and might put people off, so we intend to remove it.
segments.sourceText: We also had a question asking each trader for their exact annual income. It doesn’t answer our revised question and might put people off, so we intend to remove it.

segments.spokenText: I agree. You can ask how they describe changes without collecting an unnecessary financial profile. Remember that an interview isn't improved merely by making it longer.
segments.sourceText: I agree. You can ask how they describe changes without collecting an unnecessary financial profile. Remember that an interview isn’t improved merely by making it longer.

segments.spokenText: Our coding categories are still provisional. We thought we'd wait until after the first interviews before deciding the final set. We have broad interests, but people may describe problems we haven't anticipated.
segments.sourceText: Our coding categories are still provisional. We thought we’d wait until after the first interviews before deciding the final set. We have broad interests, but people may describe problems we haven’t anticipated.

segments.spokenText: Yes, retain that flexibility. Keep a record of changes to the categories, though. You shouldn't quietly redefine them every time you encounter an inconvenient example.
segments.sourceText: Yes, retain that flexibility. Keep a record of changes to the categories, though. You shouldn’t quietly redefine them every time you encounter an inconvenient example.

segments.spokenText: Would it be useful to compare two of us coding the same short extract?
segments.sourceText: Would it be useful to compare two of us coding the same short extract?

segments.spokenText: Very useful, as a way to discuss interpretation rather than produce a ceremonial agreement figure. If you disagree, ask whether the categories are unclear or the account genuinely supports more than one reading. The explanation of that decision may be more valuable than an artificially neat table.

segments.spokenText: That is the end of part 3. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers.
